can you elaborate on what you mean by "settings for mints firewall"? if you have a router, then you have everything you need. there is usually no need to setup a firewall for you OS. if your computer is directly connected to your ISP via ethernet-cable, the easiest thing would be to buy a cheap router and plug it between your pc and your ISP.

BUT: if you use a normal Linux distribution like ubuntu or mint, there is absolutely NO NEED AT ALL to set up a firewall. Linux has, by default, all ports closed, so by default an attacker has zero chance to "hack" your system. you can verify this by executing this in your terminal:

netstat -tulpen | grep -v '127.0.0.1'

or, if you want to find out which programs are responsible for any open ports:

sudo netstat -tulpen | grep -v '127.0.0.1'
